sections.h2: How can I sell my Oak Creek, WI house quickly?
sections.html:
The fastest routes are a cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is, or a listing priced and prepared to move within weeks. Oak Creek is a lakeshore suburb just south of Milwaukee with a mix of owners and renters, so buyers range from families to investors. Whichever path you pick, the transfer fee, the condition report and the deed filing described below still apply.

Before you contact anyone, collect these items so offers and contracts are easy to compare:

  • Your latest tax bill, which carries the ten-digit parcel number
  • A payoff figure from your lender
  • Permit paperwork for any work done since you bought the house
  • A written list of what stays and what goes with the house
  • Your first draft of the Real Estate Condition Report answers, described below

With those in hand, ask each buyer or agent for the closing date, the fees deducted from your proceeds, and what happens if an inspection turns up a problem.

sections.h2: What is Oak Creek like, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Oak Creek sits on the southwestern shore of Lake Michigan in Milwaukee County, with Milwaukee and Greenfield to the north, South Milwaukee to the north and east, Caledonia to the south, and Franklin and Greendale to the west. The town was carved out of the Town of Lake in 1840. In 1955, while it was still semi-rural, residents incorporated it as a city under a state law nicknamed the Oak Creek Law, written to keep Milwaukee from annexing it. Those details come from Wikipedia's Oak Creek entry.

Carrollville, a lakeshore neighborhood, grew around a distillery and later a glue factory that closed in 1985, and the city has since pursued cleanup and redevelopment there. More recent growth centers on Drexel Town Square, an 85-acre site built on part of the old AC Spark Plug factory grounds, with shops, restaurants, housing, a hotel and the civic center.

Today the city's business page points to direct access to I-94 and the nearby Milwaukee airport. Its home page reports a Community Partnership Agreement with Buc-ee's for a $65 million travel center, a Derse headquarters that broke ground in Oakview Business Park in August, and a Millwood Glen housing development by Veridian Homes. New construction matters to a seller because it gives buyers newer alternatives to compare against your house.

sections.h2: How fast has Oak Creek grown?
sections.html:
Oak Creek has added residents in every Census count since 1960, and the Census Bureau estimates 38,296 people on July 1, 2025, up 4.9 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. That is the only growth above 1 percent among the four cities in the Census comparison.

sections.h2: What do Oak Creek's housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Owners occupy a bit more than half of the city's housing units, and the rest are renter-occupied. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures for Oak Creek show:

  • 57.5 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, across 15,728 households
  • A median owner-occupied home value of $331,700
  • Median monthly owner costs of $1,922 with a mortgage and $838 without one
  • A median gross rent of $1,452
  • A median household income of $96,555
  • 12.1 percent of residents born outside the United States, and 17.1 percent of residents age 5 and over speaking a language other than English at home

sections.h2: Which school district covers Oak Creek, and what do city permits involve?
sections.html:
The Oak Creek-Franklin Joint School District serves all of the City of Oak Creek and a seven-square-mile part of Franklin. Its About Us page lists seven elementary schools: Carollton, Cedar Hills, Deerfield, Edgewood, Forest Ridge, Meadowview and Shepard Hills.

For permits, the city's Inspection Services page says the office handles permits for new construction and alterations, plus plumbing, electrical and heating and air conditioning installs. To book an inspection, call 414-766-7002 with your permit number and a contact name. Inspections are scheduled in morning (9 a.m. to noon) or afternoon (noon to 3 p.m.) blocks, and the city does not honor same-day requests. Status updates appear on BS&A Online when you search by address.

If an earlier owner skipped a permit, a buyer's inspector may flag it. Call Inspection Services at 414-766-7002 to learn what the file shows, and decide whether to close out the permit or disclose the gap.

sections.h2: How do I pay Oak Creek property taxes at or before closing?
sections.html:
Oak Creek's Property Tax Payments page lists four ways to pay: online through the Milwaukee County portal with the ten-digit parcel number from your bill, by mail, in person at City Hall, or at partner bank branches through January 31. The online processor charges 2.55 percent for cards with a $2 minimum, or $1.50 for an e-check. From February 1 through July 31, mailed payments go to the Treasurer, City of Oak Creek, 8040 S 6th Street.

Ask your closing agent how the current bill will be prorated, and ask the Oak Creek treasurer's office for a statement of what is owed on your parcel, including any special charges, so the figure at closing matches the city's records.

sections.h2: What must I tell a buyer, and what does the Wisconsin transfer fee cost?
sections.html:
Sellers of homes with one to four units give the buyer a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. Wis. Stat. 709.02 lets a buyer who misses that deadline rescind within two business days after it, with deposits returned. Court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived in the property and fee-exempt transfers are excused by Wis. Stat. 709.01.

The state transfer fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22, charged to the seller and collected by the register of deeds. A $330,000 sale produces a $990 fee. Add the $30 recording charge. At the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, the office takes cash, check or money order only, requires the electronic transfer return receipt for every conveyance, records documents in the order received within three to five business days, and mails them back in one to two weeks. Questions go to 414-278-4005 or RODrecordings@milwaukeecountywi.gov, per the county's recording page.

faqs.q: Does Milwaukee County accept a card for recording a deed?
faqs.a: No. The county's recording page says it accepts cash, checks or money orders made payable to the Register of Deeds, and no credit or debit cards. The $30 recording fee applies per document, and any transfer fee shown on your electronic return receipt is paid at the same time.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Oak Creek house if the owner has died?
faqs.a: Often yes, but the paperwork depends on how title was held. When a spouse has died, the county describes the Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110) with a $30 fee and an exemption under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). A personal representative selling an estate home should confirm authority with the probate court or an attorney first.

faqs.q: How long does Oak Creek take to schedule a building inspection?
faqs.a: The city asks for a call to 414-766-7002 with your permit number, and it will not do same-day inspections. Requests are filled in order received and staff availability, in morning or afternoon blocks, so book early.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report for an Oak Creek foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: A transfer that is exempt from the transfer fee is also excused from the report under Wis. Stat. 709.01. A foreclosure or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder is one of the exempt transfers in Wis. Stat. 77.25(14). If you are an owner selling voluntarily before foreclosure, the report requirement applies.

faqs.q: Which Oak Creek office can tell me what I owe in property tax?
faqs.a: The City Treasurer at City Hall handles tax payments and can confirm balances for your parcel. The city's tax page lists in-person hours of 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday, with limited check-only service in December and January.
